project.title: The barbershop on Maple Street where the line starts before sunrise and nobody minds waiting because the stories are free to hear
project.offer: A barbershop with a booking page

shots.description: People wait in a long line outside the barbershop at sunrise.
shots.line: Every Saturday the line outside Jack's started before sunrise.

shots.description: Neighbours chat in line while a child counts the people ahead.
shots.line: Nobody minded waiting, because the stories in line were half the fun.

shots.description: Marcus the barber smiles and lifts the clippers.
shots.line: Marcus unlocked the door and fired up the clippers with a grin.

shots.description: Tony reads his phone, eyebrows raised.
shots.line: Tony checked the booking page and froze.

shots.description: Dre points a finger, sure of himself.
shots.line: Dre swore he had booked two people at two o'clock.

shots.description: Dre explains with both hands up.
shots.line: Then the messages started flying in from every direction.

shots.description: A boy sits in the chair while a friend trims his hair.
shots.line: Little Jay waited his turn with a very serious face.

shots.description: A hand reaches for a glowing phone in a dark room.
shots.line: That night one phone lit up on the bedside table.

shots.description: Dre looks surprised and delighted at the news.
shots.line: By morning everyone knew a clean booking page fixes it.

shots.description: Dre shrugs, relieved, as the line moves.
shots.line: So Marcus put one link on the door and the line got shorter.
